key_insight: The paper introduces an unfitted boundary algebraic equation method for 2D Stokes flow on irregular geometries that uses lattice Green’s functions and Calderón preconditioning to solve boundary problems accurately without artificial outer boundaries or singular quadrature.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical high-order solver for incompressible flow around complex shapes, with strong robustness for exterior domains, narrow gaps, and multiply connected geometries.
method: Constructs velocity/pressure lattice Green’s functions from free-space Laplace LGFs on a staggered MAC grid.
Enforces Dirichlet boundary data at cut points via local interpolation and uses rank updates to remove hydrostatic null modes.
Solves the dense boundary system with GMRES plus a discrete Calderón preconditioner accelerated by padded FFT volume convolutions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive tests showing second-order velocity and pressure convergence, solver-accuracy discrete incompressibility, correct Moffatt eddy scaling, and condition-number reductions of orders of magnitude.
watch_item: The Calderón-preconditioned system is more demanding in narrow-gap and fine-grid interior cases, so performance may be less uniform than in exterior configurations.
paper_title: An unfitted boundary algebraic equation method with Calderón preconditioning for 2D Stokes flow in irregular geometry
